subject: AlphaCorp POC — deployment tradeoffs & dedicated sizing next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Leung <sam.leung@alphacorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: AlphaCorp POC — deployment tradeoffs & dedicated sizing next steps

Hi Sam — great meeting this morning. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on so we have alignment before we size a Dedicated SKU: 

1) Deployment choice the team is leaning to: Dedicated capacity (reserved pool) to meet predictable peak daytime traffic and stricter data controls. They still want an option to fall back to Hosted for overflow.

2) Target throughput: we heard "120 sustained TPS during business hours, with spikes to ~600 TPS for ~10m bursts" (chat + generation workloads). Please confirm if those numbers are the final ask.

3) Token mix & session behavior: per your notes — average prompt ~300 tokens, average generated response ~180 tokens (combined avg ~480). Top-10% of requests go up to 2,000 tokens. Around 40% of requests are short reranking/embedding calls (low token).

4) Model preference: you mentioned wanting an LLM comparable to 13B–33B family for price/quality tradeoffs. We should review quantized variants vs FP16 on H100/A100.

Next steps we agreed: 
- You to share the example workload CSV (samples of traffic across day + token lengths).
- Redwood to propose 2 sizing strawmen (cost-optimized and latency-optimized) that show GPU choice (A100 80GB vs H100 80GB), baseline TPS/concurrency per-GPU, and estimated monthly committed cost.
- Short (30-min) follow-up on Wed to review the strawmen.

Attachments: please attach the workload sample you mentioned. We attached our POC pricing doc for reference.

Thanks — I’ll draft the sizing assumptions and loop back to schedule Wed.

—
Ben Carter
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0189

Thanks Ben — that recap looks right. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- The 120 TPS is our sustained average across our US daytime region (09:00–18:00 PT). Spikes are primarily triggered by marketing campaigns (~10–15 mins), not continuous.
- The 40% low-token calls are an experimental feature right now; we expect that to stabilize around 30% by week 6 of the POC.
- For model family, we're fine starting on a 13B-class quantized model for cost checks but want the option to test 33B FP16 for quality-sensitive routes.

I attached the CSV sample (traffic_by_minute + token_histogram). Also looping in procurement later this week for contract terms.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Leung <sam.leung@alphacorp.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AlphaCorp POC — deployment tradeoffs & dedicated sizing next steps

Appreciate the quick clarifications and the CSV, Sam — that helps a lot. High-level thoughts (I’ll formalize into the strawmen doc before the Wed sync):

- Sizing assumptions we’ll use: average request = 480 tokens, tail to 2,000 tokens; mixed traffic with 30–40% low-token calls. KV cache will help for conversational flows that have repeated prefixes.

- GPU tradeoffs (quick summary):
  • A100 80GB FP16 — slightly cheaper per-hour, good for quantized 13B/33B variants; expected sustained throughput per-GPU for 13B-quantized ~140–200 TPS (depending on batching and prefix cache); latency SLOs slightly higher.
  • H100 80GB FP16 — better for larger FP16 33B runs and for lower latency at higher concurrency; expected sustained throughput per-GPU for 13B-quantized ~180–260 TPS and for 33B-FP16 higher headroom.

- Concurrency & batching: to hit sustained 120 TPS with <150ms median generation latency, we’ll advise configuring conservative batching (max batch 16), continuous batching enabled, and a warm KV cache for the most common prefixes. For burst coverage to ~600 TPS, we’ll propose a 2-tier pool: reserved steady capacity sized for sustained loads + burst pool (on-demand or pre-warmed spare GPUs) with a short autoscale policy.

I’ll attach two strawmen in a PDF: 
A) Cost-optimized — more quantization, A100-heavy, smaller reserved pool + slightly higher expected latency on tail.
B) Latency-optimized — H100-heavy, larger reserved pool, lower overall latency and higher burst headroom.

Proposed Wed slot: 2027-04-28 09:00 PT — does that work?

—
Ben
Attachment: redwood_dedicated_pricing_v2.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: AlphaCorp sizing strawman — please review before Wed

Marissa / Priya — internal note before the call with Sam at 09:00 PT tomorrow. I sketched the numbers below; can you sanity-check the per-GPU TPS estimates and the burst pool approach? We need two clean slides for the deck.

Assumptions (from Sam): 120 sustained TPS; 600 TPS short bursts (~10–15m); avg token payload 480; 30–40% low-token calls. Model family: start 13B-quant -> optionally test 33B-FP16.

Strawman A (cost-optimized):
- GPUs: A100 80GB (quantized models)
- Reserved pool: 6 GPUs -> estimated reserved sustained capacity ~6 * 180 TPS = 1,080 TPS theoretical; with ops overhead and concurrency splits we size to give 140 effective TPS steady -> covers 120 TPS with buffer.
- Burst pool: 2 spare GPUs pre-warmed + on-demand autoscale up to additional 6 GPUs (cooldown 10m).
- Monthly committed: see attached pricing (use tier B commit).

Strawman B (latency-optimized):
- GPUs: H100 80GB (FP16 for 33B tests)
- Reserved pool: 4 GPUs -> estimated per-GPU effective TPS 220 -> 4 * 220 = 880 theoretical; sizing gives headroom for concurrency and lower tail latency for gen routes.
- Burst pool: 4 spare GPUs pre-warmed + on-demand up to 8 additional GPUs.

Open questions:
- Do we recommend mixing GPU types in the same pool or split by route (quality-sensitive routes pinned to H100)? My bias is split pools by route for predictable latency.
- What quantization profiles should we propose for the 13B run to hit the cost-optimized numbers? Priya, could you include the suggested quantization (INT8 vs FP16) and expected perf deltas?

If this looks good I’ll finalize the two-slide summary and the costing table before the Wed call.

Thanks —
Ben
